b2-65.title: My Brother Wants Fame
b2-65.story: At breakfast, Taras announced that he was going to become a famous [[youtuber]]. Last month he had wanted to be a [[tiktoker]], but now he said short dances were not his style. He borrowed Anna's old phone and filmed his first [[vlog]] about his school day. Max, who follows a [[vlogger]] from Lviv, gave him some tips about light and sound. Then Taras decided that a [[prank video]] would get more views, so he hid a plastic spider in Dad's shoe. Dad screamed, laughed, and called him the biggest [[prankster]] in the family. In the end, the video got only twelve views, mostly from the grandparents. Still, Taras was happy, and he celebrated by downloading a new [[sticker pack]] with dancing spiders.

b2-66.title: Interviewing a Blogger
b2-66.story: For a school assignment, Anna and Lisa had to interview someone who works online. Lisa wrote to a [[food blogger]] who reviews cafés in Kyiv, but she never answered. Anna tried a [[fashion blogger]], a [[travel blogger]], and even a [[beauty blogger]] with a huge audience, but they were all too busy. Then Ira mentioned that her cousin is a [[video blogger]] who films short documentaries about small towns. He also calls himself a [[lifestyle blogger]] because he talks about cooking, books, and slow mornings. "I'm not really an [[influencer]]," he told them on a video call. "I just share things I find interesting." The girls turned the interview into a [[blogpost]] for the school website. A week later, Ira's cousin shared a link to it on his [[travel blog]], and their teacher was very impressed.

b2-67.title: Grandpa's Old Music Collection
b2-67.story: While cleaning the attic, Anna found a box of Grandpa's old music. Every [[compact disc]] was still in its original case, and some even had price labels on them. There was also an [[audio disc]] from a language course that Grandma had used in the nineties. Anna's favorite album had a [[bonus track]] that she had never heard online. Her laptop had no disc drive, so Max brought an external one and opened a free [[media player]]. When the music started, Grandpa said it sounded better than on his old [[audio player]]. Max copied everything onto a drive with one [[terabyte]] of space, which was far more than they needed. Grandpa laughed and said his first computer had only a few hundred [[kilobytes|kilobyte]] of memory. Finally, Anna saved a [[preset]] with extra bass for Grandpa's favorite songs, and he listened to them all evening.

b2-68.title: Mom's First Office Day
b2-68.story: On Monday, Anna's mom started a new job at an insurance company. At the entrance, a security guard gave her a [[badge]] with her photo on it. She had worried about the [[dress code]], but most people were wearing jeans and simple sweaters. The [[office manager]], a cheerful woman named Olena, showed her the kitchen and the [[meeting room]]. Next, someone from [[HR]] asked her to sign a few forms about her salary and vacation days. Her [[supervisor]] gave her a [[checklist]] for her first week and a thick folder with every company [[guideline]]. Mom was going to work in the [[back office]], handling documents rather than talking to customers. By lunchtime, a colleague had already told her she was a real [[ace]] with spreadsheets. That evening, she told the family that her first day had gone much better than she had expected.

b2-69.title: Sofia's First Big Client
b2-69.story: Last year, Max's sister Sofia left her job in the public [[sector]] to try [[freelance]] design. Being a [[freelancer]] was scary at first, because work did not come every month. Last week, though, she finally got a big [[project]] from a chain of bakeries. Before she started, the [[client]] sent her a [[contract]] to read and sign. They agreed to have a [[one-on-one]] call every Friday to discuss her progress. After the first call, the manager sent her some honest [[feedback]] about the colors in her logo. Sofia made the changes and even offered [[one-to-one]] training for their staff on the new design. The bakery loved the idea, and the extra money gave her confidence a real [[boost]].

b2-70.title: Ira at the Call Center
b2-70.story: Ira got a summer job at a [[call center]] that answers questions for a phone [[service center]]. On her first shift, she worked as an [[operator]], helping customers with broken screens and lost chargers. In the morning, her computer froze, so she called the system [[administrator]]. He was busy, so another [[admin]] came over and restarted everything. He explained that a [[script]] ran every night to back up the customer records, and it had crashed. During lunch, her manager said that patience was the most important [[soft skill]] in this job. She also offered Ira some free [[coaching]] on how to calm down angry callers. In the afternoon, Ira faced a [[dilemma]]: an old man needed help, but her shift was ending. She stayed ten extra minutes, and he thanked her warmly. Just as she hung up, Anna texted that she was waiting outside with ice cream, which was perfect [[timing]].

b2-71.title: A Busy Office Week
b2-71.story: Anna's dad works on the fifth floor of a large [[business center]] near the river. This week, his [[project manager]] announced that the company was moving to a smaller office. Everyone had to clear their desks, and the old [[shredder]] worked nonstop from morning till evening. On Wednesday, a [[consultant]] arrived to help them organize the move. She had worked in [[consulting]] for twenty years and seemed to have a solution for every problem. On Thursday, she ran a short [[seminar]] about working in shared spaces. At the end, she handed out a colorful [[booklet]] with tips on keeping desks tidy. Dad brought it home, and Mom joked that he should read it twice.

b2-72.title: Our New Startup
b2-72.story: Max and Anna decided to launch a small [[startup]] that delivers homemade snacks to students. Max called himself the [[founder]], but Anna reminded him that the idea was hers. They spent a weekend writing a [[business plan]] at Grandma's kitchen table. Their [[business model]] was simple: students would pay a small monthly fee for weekly deliveries. The only problem was that they had almost no [[capital]], just their savings from summer jobs. Then Grandma offered to bake the cookies herself and become their [[business partner]]. After the first month, they made a tiny [[profit]] of about fifty dollars. Grandma said it was a [[win-win]] deal: they got great cookies, and she got two helpers in her garden.
